translation_notes: the single term read becomes an island inside the tuple handed to graph.remove: RDFS.subClassOf -> rdfs:subClassOf. There is no island for graph *removal* (g{} only builds graphs), so the remove() call and its Python tuple are untouched - the notation reaches the term, not the operation
the mechanical draft inserted the @prefix block in the middle of the parenthesised 'from rdflib import (' list, which is not valid ldpy; the declarations now sit before the imports

'from rdflib import (...)' is left untouched even though RDFS becomes unused inside the region (the demo harness still uses it, and the extract's other imported names were already unused) - same convention as the sibling region AllClasses
the unused rdf: declaration of the draft is kept so the 1:1 correspondence with the RDF/RDFS pair of the import block stays visible

demo harness added identically to both sides: __isub__ returns an infixowl Class, which the harness cannot compare, so the demo builds A/B/C with two rdfs:subClassOf edges, retracts one through the operator, and prints the remaining subclasses; demo_graph is compared by isomorphism
